| [THEORY-020](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-020.md) | KS obstruction lies in how contexts overlap | Stone (1936, 1937), [LIT-353](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-353.md) and [LIT-358](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-358.md): every Boolean ring is isomorphic to the compact open sets of its prime-ideal space, a totally disconnected, locally compact Hausdorff space that is compact exactly when there is a unit, and every such space arises this way. Kochen & Specker ([LIT-298](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-298.md), Thm 0) turn this into the criterion that a partial Boolean algebra embeds in a Boolean one iff its two-valued homomorphisms separate points. The joining of the two, that non-classicality needs more than one context, is the record's. Neither Stone paper uses "ultrafilter" or states a duality of categories. | Active |
| [THEORY-024](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-024.md) v2 | Global sections restore classical Boolean logic | Ghose (2025), [LIT-276](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-276.md) — asserts that the Heyting algebra of truth values "becomes Boolean" when the presheaf data collapse to a global section, and that sheaves encode Boolean reasoning. Both claims are asserted, not proved. The record's readings refute them. The internal logic of a topos is fixed by the base category and its topology, not by whether one presheaf has a section (Isham–Butterfield, [LIT-325](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-325.md), §6). Sheaf toposes such as Sh(ℝ) are not Boolean ([NOTE-249](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-249.md)). The contextuality criterion itself is untouched. | Rejected |
| [THEORY-037](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-037.md) v3 | Topos quantum logic is Heyting, not orthomodular | Döring & Isham (2007, II), [LIT-335](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-335.md) — daseinisation maps each projector injectively to a clopen sub-object of the spectral presheaf, with δ(P∨Q) = δ(P)∨δ(Q) but only δ(P∧Q) ⪯ δ(P)∧δ(Q). The orthocomplement is carried to inner daseinisation, not to ¬δ(P). That Sub_cl(Σ) is Heyting (Thm 2.5) is sketched in the source, and the record re-derives it: each Σ_V is extremally disconnected, so Sub_cl(Σ) is a frame. Paper I ([LIT-343](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-343.md)) chooses intuitionistic deduction. Isham–Butterfield ([LIT-325](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-325.md)) state that the Heyting algebra is fixed by the base category. | Active |
| [THEORY-041](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-041.md) | Quantum logic began modular, not orthomodular | Birkhoff & von Neumann (1936), [LIT-306](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-306.md) — the lattice of closed subspaces is orthocomplemented and not distributive. They propose modularity (L5), motivated by a dimension function, and give an explicit infinite-dimensional pentagon that breaks it. The word "orthomodular" does not occur. Husimi (1937), [LIT-357](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-357.md), derives modularity as the parallelogram law under a finite-chain assumption and uses the orthomodular identity as a step without naming it. Citing either paper for "the orthomodular lattice of quantum logic" misattributes it. | Active |
| [THEORY-042](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-042.md) | Cross-sector superposition is operationally mixed | Wick, Wightman & Wigner (1952), [LIT-339](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-339.md) — they define a superselection rule and show that a superposition across sectors "is not a pure state, but a statistical mixture". They prove the rule from time reversal for integer versus half-integer angular momentum, and postulate it for charge with "no conclusive evidence". What follows for Birkhoff–von Neumann's lattice ([LIT-306](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-306.md)), a product of sector lattices with central sector projections, is the record's inference. The centre-of-the-algebra formulation belongs to Haag, who is not read. | Active |
| [THEORY-127](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-127.md) v5 | Robust group judgments can't be propositionwise | List & Pettit (2006), [LIT-705](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-705.md): under universal domain, robust group rationality (complete, consistent, deductively closed group judgments for every profile of rational member judgments) is inconsistent with majoritarian, uniform proposition-wise and proposition-wise supervenience (Propositions 1–3; the last two proved elsewhere and cited), and consistent with set-wise supervenience, which the premise-based and distributed premise-based procedures achieve (Propositions 4–5). Members' judgments on a conclusion can then be insufficient, or even unnecessary, to fix the group's judgment on it. List (2014), [LIT-700](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-700.md), makes this the mark of a third kind of collective attitude: corporate attitudes, a group agent's, supervene "holistically", while aggregate and common attitudes supervene proposition by proposition. Active since 2026-10-19 for categorical judgments on the court agenda and on agendas with two stated connectedness conditions: the record re-derived Proposition 3 (and Proposition 2 as a corollary) itself. The extension to corporate attitudes in general is QUESTION-152. | Active |
| [THEORY-162](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-162.md) | Context change is part of meaning | Heim (1982), [LIT-838](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-838.md); Veltman (1996), [LIT-818](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-818.md); Krifka (2024), [LIT-835](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-835.md). Three readings find, each in its own domain, sentences that agree in truth conditions or in the proposition they carry but differ in their effect on a conversational state. The effects are anaphoric potential (Heim), tests rather than information (Veltman), and changing indices rather than eliminating them (Krifka). This is the dynamic view: meaning as context-change potential. It does not say that truth conditions are irrelevant, since each framework recovers them, or that the three formalisms agree with each other. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-255](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-255.md) v4 | Meet and join can't overextend concepts | Aerts (2009), [LIT-934](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-934.md), Theorem 9 and §§2.2–3.3, read in full in [NOTE-808](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-808.md). The impossibility is a proof, and it needs only that membership is monotone in the subspace. The fits that place the k-type deviations in a tilted subspace lattice and the ∆-type ones in an emergent sector are models with free parameters, not tests. Negation appears only as the orthocomplement used to derive the conjunction model from the disjunction model; no negated concept is measured. | Active |
| [THEORY-341](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-341.md) | Negation as failure deduces only in two cases | Clark (1978), [LIT-1087](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1087.md), read in [NOTE-894](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-894.md), and Reiter (1978), [LIT-1088](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1088.md), read in [NOTE-899](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-899.md) from his 1977 workshop report. Clark proves negation as failure sound with respect to the completed database (the clauses read as if-and-only-if definitions, plus axioms that distinct names denote distinct things), given a finite failure tree for some selection rule; it is incomplete in general. Reiter defines the closed-world assumption by entailment, reduces closed-world query evaluation to open-world atomic queries when the assumption is consistent, and shows it consistent for Horn and definite databases but not for Pa ∨ Pb. Soundness here is relative to the completion, not to the world, and neither paper says anything about a search cut short by time. | Active |
| [THEORY-347](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-347.md) | Equivalent belief bases can revise differently | Hansson's Stanford Encyclopedia survey (2006, revised 2026), [LIT-1072](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1072.md), read in [NOTE-866](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-866.md), with Alchourrón, Gärdenfors and Makinson (1985), [LIT-1050](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1050.md), read in [NOTE-874](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-874.md). Bases {p, q} and {p, p ↔ q} have one closure, yet revised by ¬p one yields q and the other ¬q: statically but not dynamically equivalent. Base contraction escapes the Recovery that AGM proves for closed theories, and many inconsistent bases exist where there is one inconsistent closed set. A base marks which beliefs are held in their own right and recomputes the rest; it is not a record of reasons, sources or defeated alternatives, and the survey gives no result that bases handle iterated revision better. | Active |
| [THEORY-353](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-353.md) | AGM contractions are partial meet contractions | Alchourrón, Gärdenfors and Makinson (1985), [LIT-1050](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1050.md), read in [NOTE-874](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-874.md), with Hansson's survey, [LIT-1072](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1072.md), read in [NOTE-866](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-866.md). Contracting a closed theory A by x keeps what a selected set of maximal x-free subsets of A share; the six basic postulates characterize exactly these partial meet contractions (Observation 2.5), and with the two supplementary postulates exactly those selected by a transitive relation (Corollary 4.5). Revision follows by the Levi identity. A selection function or ordering must be added to A, and in the finite case distinct ones give distinct contractions. Nothing here concerns iterated change, where the selection comes from, or why a belief is held. | Active |
| [THEORY-362](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-362.md) v2 | Derivation counts maintain views incrementally | Gupta, Mumick and Subrahmanian (1993), [LIT-1114](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1114.md), read in [NOTE-915](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-915.md). Algorithm 4.1 evaluates delta rules in order of rule stratum and combines signed counts; Theorem 4.1 states it derives count(t^ν) − count(t) for every tuple, and Theorems 6.1 and 6.2 extend this to negated and aggregate subgoals. Its cost is argued to be close to evaluating the view and is not measured. All three theorems are stated without proof in this extended abstract. It does not say that a count suffices when support is cyclic: the paper keeps counting to nonrecursive views. | Active |
| [THEORY-367](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-367.md) v3 | Minimal witnesses are query-invariant | Buneman, Khanna and Tan (2001), [LIT-1104](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1104.md), read in [NOTE-920](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-920.md). Two meanings of the provenance of output data: why it is there (the witness basis, the source structures matched by each valuation that produces it) and where a value came from (the source paths bound to the output variable). The first is preserved by the paper's rewrite system and, cut down to minimal witnesses, agrees across equivalent queries with equality conditions; the second is shown by example to depend on how the query is written. Proofs are omitted. It is not a theory of revision: additions to the source, negation, aggregation and strengths of support are all outside it. | Active |
| [THEORY-371](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-371.md) | CQ equivalence is homomorphism both ways | Chandra and Merlin (1977), [LIT-1111](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1111.md), read in [NOTE-907](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-907.md). Reading a conjunctive query as its natural model, equivalence becomes a pair of homomorphisms (Lemma 13), the minimal equivalent query is unique up to isomorphism (Theorem 12), and evaluation with the query as input is NP-complete (Theorem 7), as is deciding whether one query is a folding of another (Theorem 11). The paper states equivalence, not containment, and does not state that containment or equivalence is NP-complete; those are corollaries later work attributes to it. Nothing here reaches queries with equality, comparisons, negation or union. | Active |
| [THEORY-373](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-373.md) | Semiring provenance factors through polynomials | Green, Karvounarakis and Tannen (2007), [LIT-1110](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1110.md), read in [NOTE-913](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-913.md). Union and projection add tags, join multiplies them; the usual RA identities hold exactly when the tags form a commutative semiring, and a map of tags commutes with every query exactly when it is a semiring homomorphism. The polynomials N[X] are the free commutative semiring, so the annotated answer in any semiring is the polynomial answer evaluated at the input annotations (Theorem 4.3). It is a sufficiency result for revisions that re-annotate existing inputs, not a minimality result, and it excludes added facts and every nonmonotone operation. | Active |
| [THEORY-374](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-374.md) v2 | Exact view answerability is NP-complete | Halevy (2001), [LIT-1116](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1116.md), read in [NOTE-921](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-921.md), reporting Levy et al. 1995 ([LIT-1100](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1100.md), read), Duschka, Genesereth and Levy, and Abiteboul and Duschka 1998 (not read). Reuse of stored views is graded: certifying an exact rewriting is NP-complete in the size of the definitions, building everything the views give (maximally contained) is polynomial, and the certain answers can cost a co-NP-hard search in the size of the stored data. Promoted 2026-10-21 on a re-derivation of the last two parts (ADR-047 v2); the primary papers they come from are unread. None of it prices recognition for definitions outside conjunctive queries and datalog, or says how costly recognition is on typical queries. | Active |
| [THEORY-380](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-380.md) v3 | Datalog provenance is formal power series | Green, Karvounarakis and Tannen (2007), [LIT-1110](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1110.md), read in [NOTE-913](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-913.md). A recursive query can derive a tuple in infinitely many ways, so polynomials do not suffice and the semiring needs infinite sums. With ω-continuous semirings and the provenance semiring N∞⟦X⟧ the paper states the analogues of the relational results: a fixed-point characterization (Theorem 5.6), factorization (Theorem 6.4), and a test for infinite coefficients (Theorem 6.5), with algorithms that decide finiteness and compute coefficients. Proofs are not given. Plain N and N[X] are excluded, the provenance can be an infinite object held only as equations, and negation remains outside. | Active |
| [THEORY-387](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-387.md) v3 | Delete-and-rederive maintains recursive views | Gupta, Mumick and Subrahmanian (1993), [LIT-1114](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1114.md), read in [NOTE-915](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-915.md). DRed runs stratum by stratum: semi-naive Δ⁻-rules compute an overestimate of deletions, δ⁺-rules put back those with a derivation in the reduced database, and Δ⁺-rules add insertions. Theorem 7.1 states the result contains t if and only if t has a derivation in (E − Δ⁻) ∪ Δ⁺; the proof is in a 1992 AT&T report the record has not seen. The paper asserts, and does not show, that DRed handles stratified negation, aggregation and rule changes, that it beats the PF algorithm by up to an order of magnitude, and that it is slower than counting on nonrecursive views. | Active |
| [THEORY-389](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-389.md) | Rewriting queries using views is NP-complete | Levy, Mendelzon, Sagiv and Srivastava (1995), [LIT-1100](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1100.md), read in [NOTE-909](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-909.md). Every use of a view in an equivalent rewriting comes from a containment mapping from the view into the query (Proposition 3.1); without comparisons a locally minimal complete rewriting has at most as many literals as the query (Lemma 3.5), which puts the problems in NP, and they are NP-complete (Theorems 3.7, 3.9, 3.10), with two independent sources of hardness. The results are worst case, in the size of the definitions rather than the stored data, for equivalent rewritings under set semantics only; they do not say recognizing reuse is costly in practice, and they do not cover contained (partial) rewritings. | Active |
| [THEORY-462](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-462.md) v2 | Monotonic logic can't represent displaced defaults | Minsky (1974), the frames memo, [LIT-410](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-410.md), read in [NOTE-337](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-337.md). Its appendix argues that "logistic" systems fail for commonsense on five counts, of which monotonicity is a correct observation about classical logic. That no repair is possible is asserted ("I think such attempts will continue to fail"), and consistency being undesirable is argued by analogy. The reading says the memo is a source of hypotheses, not evidence; this account takes from it only the half that holds by definition and marks the rest as the memo's claim. Active as the definitional half and a report of how the memo supports the rest; the further claim is THEORY-1239, Proposed. | Active |
| [THEORY-493](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-493.md) | Three axiom pairings yield GEM; Simons' doesn't | Varzi, SEP "Mereology" (2003, revised June 2026), [LIT-124](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-124.md), read in full in [NOTE-163](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-163.md). The record has not checked the proofs. It is stated for first-order theories with a single primitive P and infinitary principles as axiom schemas, and it is a fact about axiom systems: it does not say classical mereology is true of anything. | Active |
| [THEORY-516](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-516.md) | Base category, not global sections, fixes logic | Butterfield & Isham (1998), [LIT-381](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-381.md), read in full in [NOTE-329](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-329.md): Theorem 4.1 proves that generalized FUNC is exactly naturality of ν : G → Ω, for any presheaf G of posets on any small category. In classical physics the value presheaf has a global section per microstate (3.6–3.7), yet the macrostate and microstate valuations are sieve-valued, and [NOTE-329](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-329.md) shows excluded middle failing at a microstate. Isham & Butterfield (1999), [LIT-389](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-389.md) ([NOTE-334](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-334.md)), adds that Ω is unique for a given topos and that a base with one arrow between any two objects gives two-valued logic. The choice of base, and so of the logic, remains free. | Active |
| [THEORY-535](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-535.md) | Quasi-sets count indistinguishable particles | Holik, Jorge, Krause & Lombardi (2021), [LIT-107](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-107.md), read in full from the preprint in [NOTE-127](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-127.md). The Lombardi–da Costa ontology of properties makes a quantum system a bundle of instances of universal type-properties, with no principle of individuality. Krause's quasi-set theory Q, reinterpreted over property-instances, represents an atomic bundle as a qset taking one instance from each qset of indiscernibles, guaranteed by Q's Axiom of Choice, and N particles as a subqset of quasi-cardinal N. The new formal content is about two pages (§6), the printed proofs contain errors, and states, actualization and dynamics are not formalized. The claims about Kochen–Specker and non-separability are recharacterizations by definition, not results. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-544](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-544.md) | Segal condition makes types category-like | Riehl & Shulman (2017), [LIT-032](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-032.md), read in full in [NOTE-069](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-069.md). The internal results of §§5–11 are proved: associativity from the Segal condition applied to A^2 (Prop. 5.9), inner 3-horns (Prop. 5.21), functoriality of every function (Prop. 6.1), the dependent Yoneda lemma (Thm 9.5), and uniqueness of left adjoints into a Segal type from a Rezk type (Thm 11.23). Segal and Rezk types match Segal and complete Segal spaces (Props A.21, A.25), but soundness of the type theory in bisimplicial sets is sketched and depends on an unproved initiality theorem. Coherence in all dimensions is conjectured, not proved. | Active |
| [THEORY-595](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-595.md) | Ultrafilter extension is Lindenbaum's lemma | Turner (preprint 2021, published 2025), [LIT-145](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-145.md), read in [NOTE-177](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-177.md). An expository paper: "None of the results are novel" (p. 2). Maximal, prime and ultra filters coincide (Thm 2); every filter extends to an ultrafilter (Thm 3); Łoś's theorem (Thm 9); compactness (Thm 12). The results are standard and correct, though the write-up has slips. A filter is only finitely consistent, and that is the point. The pairings with Lindenbaum and Henkin are analogies, not reductions. | Active |
| [THEORY-619](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-619.md) | Coarse-graining is direct image of clopens | Butterfield & Isham (2001), "Topos Perspective on the Kochen-Specker Theorem: IV", [LIT-382](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-382.md), read in full in [NOTE-328](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-328.md). §2.4 proves G ≅ CloΣ: restricting the characters of V₁ that make P̂ true gives exactly the characters of V₂ that make its coarse-graining true, via a cited state-extension theorem. | [THEORY-642](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-642.md) | Two-level type theory is conservative over HoTT | Annenkov, Capriotti, Kraus & Sattler (2017; MSCS 2023), [LIT-095](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-095.md), whose §§1–3 were read in full in [NOTE-047](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-047.md), the reading of the nLab page it supersedes ([LIT-040](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-040.md)). Results that use the axioms relating the two levels' natural numbers, which untruncated semisimplicial types need, are not known to transfer. | Active |
| [THEORY-647](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-647.md) v2 | Ultraclose credence dissolves the lottery paradox | Wenmackers (2011), [LIT-163](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-163.md), chapter 3, read in [NOTE-139](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-139.md). That belief works this way is argued: any explicit threshold collapses the model back to the Lockean one, the author calls it "crude", and knowledge is set aside. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-649](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-649.md) v2 | Peer averaging often leaves someone inconsistent | Wenmackers (2011), [LIT-163](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-163.md), chapter 5, read in [NOTE-139](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-139.md). The per-agent fraction F_AG peaks at 1.8112% (M = 2) and 0.3215% (M = 3); the per-profile fraction F_OP reaches 6.4298% and 16.867%. The thesis's headline, that the risk "can be made arbitrarily small" by adding sentences, rests on two values of M and is contradicted for F_OP. | Active |
| [THEORY-665](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-665.md) v2 | Assertion is commitment in deontic scorekeeping | Brandom (1994), [LIT-794](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-794.md), skimmed in [NOTE-622](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-622.md): the Preface and the core of chapter 3 only. | [THEORY-698](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-698.md) v2 | Probe lattices are guaranteed by construction | Xiong (2026), [LIT-267](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-267.md), read in [NOTE-240](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-240.md). | [THEORY-725](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-725.md) v2 | Premise-based voting is robustly rational | List & Pettit (2006), [LIT-705](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-705.md), read in full in [NOTE-550](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-550.md), for the court agenda only. Proposition 4: the premise-based procedure, majorities on P, Q and the biconditional with R derived, is robustly rational and makes the group's set a function of the members' sets. Under it the members' judgments on R do not fix the group's (weak discontinuity), and under the distributed procedure they need not enter (strong discontinuity, Proposition 5). The general impossibility for proposition-wise rules is [THEORY-127](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-127.md), still Proposed. | Active |

| [THEORY-1064](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1064.md) v2 | Spurious counterexamples locate missing splits | Clarke, Grumberg, Jha, Lu and Veith (2000), [LIT-1652](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1652.md), read in [NOTE-1231](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1231.md) from the authors' manuscript of the CAV paper. Common knowledge of a fact is the greatest fixed point of everyone knowing the fact and it; a guaranteed simultaneous coordinated action makes itself common knowledge (Proposition 4); over a channel that can lose any message, no fact becomes common knowledge that was not so at the start (Theorem 5), and the same holds when start and delivery times are uncertain, even if every message arrives (Theorem 8); so no protocol guarantees coordinated attack, simultaneous or eventual (Corollary 6, Proposition 10). Filed so that claims using the result ground on a reading, not on the bare work: [CLAIM-668](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-668.md) through [ARG-097](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-097.md). The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |

| [THEORY-2308](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2308.md) | Intuitionistic logic is a calculus of problems | Kolmogorov (1932), [LIT-3229](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3229.md), read in [NOTE-2422](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2422.md) from the GDZ scan. A problem is explained by examples (p. 59), is solved and not true (p. 61, n. 8), and, fully stated, carries its permitted means (p. 59, n. 2); a ⊃ b reduces b's solution to a's, ¬a derives a contradiction from a supposed solution of a. The calculus coincides in form with Heyting's (pp. 58, 63) and does not solve a ∨ ¬a. §2: an existence statement is a problem plus its solution, and a problem's sense is independent of the state of our knowledge (p. 65). It corroborates [CLAIM-949](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-949.md)'s correspondence of a question with a problem, narrowed ([ARG-245](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-245.md)), and corrects its attribution: Kolmogorov keeps statements and problems apart.
